learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the pain of losing one's native language, the danger of procrastination, and the theme of linguistic chauvinism during wartime.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: During the Franco-Prussian war, France lost Alsace and Lorraine to Prussia. An order comes from Berlin that only German will be taught in the schools of these districts, replacing French.
Franz, a young boy who used to hate school and delay learning his mother tongue, suddenly feels a deep sense of loss and regret when he realizes this is his last French lesson.
The strict teacher, M. Hamel, wears his best clothes and delivers his last lesson with immense patience and emotion. He calls French the most beautiful and logical language in the world.

main_concepts.concept_title: 🗝️ Language as a Key to Prison
main_concepts.simple_explanation: M. Hamel emphasizes that when people are enslaved, as long as they hold fast to their native language, it is as if they have the key to their prison.
When Franz hears pigeons cooing, he wonders, 'Will they make them sing in German, even the pigeons?' This highlights the absurdity of forcing a language on living beings.

fun_activity.title: 🗣️ The Language Ban Simulation
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine you wake up tomorrow and your government bans you from speaking your mother tongue (Hindi or your regional language). Write a short 3-sentence diary entry expressing how you would feel communicating only in a foreign language.

exam_tips: 📌 Always mention 'Linguistic Chauvinism' (the aggressive and unreasonable belief that your own language is superior) when discussing the theme of the story.
📌 Describe M. Hamel's transformation: From a 'cranky' ruler-wielding teacher to a patient, deeply patriotic man on his last day.
📌 Remember the phrase 'Vive La France!' (Long Live France!) which M. Hamel wrote on the blackboard at the very end.
quick_recap: ⭐ The story is set in the days of the Franco-Prussian War (1870-1871).
⭐ The village elders (like old Hauser) sat on the back benches to show respect to M. Hamel for his 40 years of faithful service.
⭐ Franz was initially scared to go to school because he hadn't learned the rules for participles.
